source_observations.observation: The condition is the ground for applying the word. A class, quality or action can supply that ground.
Retain ordinary tva and tal alongside special routes, with further coexistence of strī and puṃs forms. The priestly terminal condition has a separate policy.
Negative determinative versus exocentric compound, three differing blocked successors, eight exceptions. The Kāśikā passage in this edition has budha.
Names yudha and gives āyudhyam in its series. Modern editorial note also explicitly identifies this difference across Kāśikā versions.
The received sūtra in the canonical register has yudha. The explanatory note documents the other reading.
Option preserves aṇ, ṣyañ or añ when licensed in addition to the common defaults. Gives ṭi loss and the treatment of ṛ in the named iman stems.
Colour qualifications and dṛḍādi allow ṣyañ and imanic. The ṣ marker provides for feminine ṅīṣ, with separate y deletion.
Four alternatives for tanu, additional feminine examples, and preverb-specific members of the quality class.
Prathimā is requested in the series with me and explained as extension. The neighbouring individual abstracts need their own derivations.
The participle dadhānena governs the accusative of bodily breadth.
The expanding qualities attain breadth. One strong accusative is shared with Bhaṭṭi despite the change of predicate.
He substitutes pṛthutvam for the accusative governed by āpuḥ, independently locating the parallel abstract in the object slot.
Mārdavam occurs among the qualities with plural bhavanti in 16.3.
Mṛdutā and freedom from cruelty explain mārdavam. Both the grammatical and ethical settings retain the same abstract.
